title: Indifferentiability of Three- and Four-Round Confusion-Diffusion Networks
summary: A distinguishing attack rules out indifferentiability from a random permutation for networks with at most two rounds; the three- and four-round cases remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For confusion-diffusion networks, a distinguishing attack establishes that networks with two rounds or fewer cannot be indifferentiable from a random permutation. No similarly general attack was found for three-round networks, leaving unresolved whether a three- or four-round confusion-diffusion network can be indifferentiable from a random permutation. The open task is therefore to determine indifferentiability for the three- and four-round cases, or, if either case is not indifferentiable, to develop a general distinguishing attack against it.

scope.domain: Indifferentiability of confusion-diffusion networks as symmetric cryptographic constructions.
parameters: Number of rounds, determining the network cases covered by the known attack and the unresolved three- and four-round cases
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine indifferentiability for the three- and four-round cases, or, if either case is not indifferentiable, develop a general distinguishing attack against it.

progress.summary: The source reports a general distinguishing attack for networks with two rounds or fewer and says that no similarly general attack was found for three rounds. It presents the three- and four-round cases as open.
citation_labels: Yevgeniy Dodis et al., Indifferentiability of Confusion-Diffusion Networks
